title: Lunara Silver "Moonlit" launch shot-board: pull eight beats from one 4K product take, neutralize each to the in-frame grey card so the board reads as one continuous grade, then data-merge one press-ready shot per page

source.reference: Video editor / short-form content for a D2C sterling-silver jewellery brand

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a growing D2C sterling-silver jewellery brand that wanted a freelance video editor to 'repurpose existing content into multiple formats and variations' for short-form and social. Laundered to a fictional brand, 'Lunara Silver', with a fictional founder persona ('Priya Nair, founder') — no real company, person, product, or trademark is named anywhere (the real source brand is NOT reproduced). REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the killed original tried to reframe an already-9:16 1080x1920 clip to 9:16 (a no-op that also would have upscaled) and shipped its 'end card' as un-composited layers the connector cannot assemble, so the agent owned nothing. The corrected design keeps the same job the brief actually rewards — turn ONE existing product take into launch-ready deliverables — but routes it to what the connectors genuinely do: the brand shot a single continuous ~40s 4K studio take of the 'Moonlit' pendant being lifted, turned in window light and clasped on the neck, and needs a PRINTED shot-board (the physical lookbook production board the studio pins up and hands to its packaging/print vendor) built from the strongest beats, plus a vertical social teaser cut of the same take. The freelancer PULLS eight key frames from the one take (a creative selection the agent owns — which beat, which sharp moment), grades each pulled still to one house look, preps them for print, vectorizes the wordmark for the board masthead, and DATA-MERGES a genuinely hand-authored single-record InDesign board template (one shot per page) into a press-ready PDF. The take's window light drifts over the ~40s (a passing cloud, the hand occasionally shadowing the piece), so the pulled beats do NOT match out of the file; a photographic 18% grey card is clipped to the linen at the frame edge throughout so every beat can be neutralized to one white point after the fact. Nothing is invented beyond the 'multiple formats / repurpose existing content' the brief calls for.
one_line_ask: Pull eight strong beats from Lunara Silver's single ~40s 4K 'Moonlit' pendant take, neutralize each pulled frame to the 18% grey card that sits in the take so the whole board reads as one continuous grade (each beat needs its own white-balance and exposure decision because the light drifts across the take), crop each to the portrait board window without upscaling, vectorize the wordmark for the masthead, then data-merge the brand's authored single-record InDesign shot-board template to produce one press-ready shot per page — plus a same-length 9:16 vertical teaser reframe of the take.
full_brief:
Lunara Silver is a growing D2C brand of handcrafted sterling-silver jewellery, and we are launching our 'Moonlit' pendant. We are NOT reshooting and we do NOT need a finished edited film here — our in-house editor cuts the hero film in Premiere. What we need from you is the production pack built off the ONE take we already have.

Here is what you are given: (1) moonlit_take_4k.mp4 — a single continuous ~40 second 4K (3840x2160) studio take, hand-held-steady, of the pendant being lifted off the linen, slowly turned so the polished silver catches the window light, a macro pass on the engraved crescent, and finally clasped and settled on the neck. Because it is one long take by a window, the light changes across it — a cloud passes partway through, and the hand shadows the piece on the macro move — so different moments in the take do NOT match each other straight out of the file: some beats are warm and bright, others go cool and dim. To make the match checkable we clipped a photographic 18% grey card onto the linen at the edge of frame, and it stays in shot the whole take. (2) lunara_shotboard_template.indd — the InDesign shot-board page we hand-built, one shot per page, with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (the shot frame and the masthead). (3) moonlit_shotlist.csv — our eight-beat shot list: the beat name, a camera note, the approximate timecode in the take, and the format tag for each of the eight shots we want on the board. (4) lunara_wordmark_flat.png — our flat wordmark on transparency, which we want razor-sharp on the board masthead.

What I need back:
- THE SHOT-BOARD (the main deliverable): a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF of our lookbook production board, ONE shot per page, eight pages, that our packaging vendor prints and pins up. For each of the eight beats on the shot list, pull the strongest, SHARP frame near that beat's timecode out of the take (if the exact timecode lands on a motion-blurred transition, step to the clean frame beside it — a soft frame prints muddy and we will reject it), grade it, and drop it into the page's shot window with its beat name, camera note, timecode and format tag bound in from the list, and our wordmark crisp in the masthead.
- THE GRADE (this is the whole craft of it): the board has to read as ONE continuous piece, not eight stills from eight different shoots. Bring every pulled frame to the SAME house look — a clean, true-to-silver grade where the neutral grey card in that frame lands truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at one common white point, and the set shares one exposure feel. Because the take's light drifts, no two beats start from the same cast or brightness, so getting all eight onto that one white point is a per-frame decision — each frame has to be neutralized to its OWN in-frame grey card, and how far and which way to move is yours to judge from that card, frame by frame. A set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will drift apart at the grey cards and we will reject it. Keep the silver reading like real metal — bright, not blown; neutral, not blue. When you are done, hand back, per frame, the white-balance (temperature / tint) and exposure move you dialed and the final pixel size, so we can confirm the board was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.
- PRINT SIZE: each board page drops the frame into a 130 x 173 mm portrait shot window, and at press resolution that window needs at least ~1535 x 2044 px of real image. The take is 4K, so a portrait crop taken from the FULL frame just clears that; a frame you graded on a small proxy, or a landscape frame stretched to fill a portrait window, will fall under and print soft — do not enlarge past what the 4K frame actually holds.
- THE TEASER: a full-length 9:16 vertical (1080x1920) reframe of the whole take for the launch-announcement story — same runtime, reframed to vertical, no trimming and no upscaling (the 4K master has the height for it).
- THE WORDMARK: our flat wordmark cleaned to a crisp SVG for the board masthead and reusable on future covers.

Keep the sources in our Creative Cloud folder. Bind the beat names, camera notes and timecodes verbatim from the shot list — do not rename our beats. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the eight pages matched to one white point with the per-frame moves reported; every board frame at least ~1535 x 2044 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the 130 x 173 mm window; the teaser exactly 1080x1920 at the take's full runtime; the wordmark crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one board page per shot-list row.

inputs.name: moonlit_take_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CAMERA ORIGINAL (declared at camera scale; no generative video model produces this length/resolution reliably, which is the point — it must be a real capture): a single continuous ~40 second 4K (3840x2160, 16:9, ~24-30fps) hand-held-steady studio take of a handcrafted sterling-silver 'moonlit' crescent pendant on a fine chain, shot beside a window. Across the one take: a hand lifts the pendant off soft linen (~00:03, sun out, warm and bright), slowly turns it so the polished silver throws a highlight (~00:08, a cloud begins to pass, light cooling and dimming), a macro push-in on the engraved crescent detail (~00:14, the hand shadows the piece, underexposed), the silver catches a returning shaft of sun (~00:19, bright with a hot specular glint on the polished metal), a slow rotation showing the back (~00:24, near-neutral but flat and low-contrast), the pendant is raised toward the neckline (~00:29, backlit, hazy and flat, slightly warm), a model clasps it at the collarbone (~00:34, cool window fill on skin, a touch dim), and it settles on the neck at rest (~00:39, low warm sun, warm and slightly dark). A photographic 18% grey card is clipped to the linen at the FAR EDGE of frame and stays visible in shot for the entire take as a white-balance reference. Real silver reflections, micro-scratches and hand-finishing marks, shallow depth of field, gentle real handheld drift, candid documentary product-video look, NOT glossy CGI, no on-screen text or captions, no real brand names or logos on any object.
inputs.realism_notes: ONE genuine ~40s 4K camera take, declared at camera scale so both downstream needs are honest: (a) frames pulled with video_render_frame are native 3840x2160 stills, so a portrait board crop taken from the FULL frame (max 1620x2160 for the 130x173mm ~3:4 window) clears the ~1535x2044 print floor without upscaling; (b) video_resize to a same-runtime 9:16 vertical holds >=1080 width from the 4K height (a 9:16 crop of 3840x2160 is ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale). The light deliberately drifts across the single take (passing cloud, hand shadow, returning sun) so the eight pulled beats start from DIFFERENT casts and exposures and cannot be matched with one blanket correction — each must be neutralized to the static in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable target. The grey card stays in shot throughout so every pulled frame carries the reference; it is cropped out of the final board crops but retained in the card-bearing masters for grade audit. The ~40s runtime is longer than any target derived from it (frame stills; a same-length reframe) and the take is a real capture, not an ~8s AI clip.

inputs.name: lunara_shotboard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 portrait (148 x 210 mm) lookbook shot-board page with 3 mm bleed — ONE shot per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<ShotNo>>, <<Beat>>, <<CameraNote>>, <<Timecode>>, <<FormatTag>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 130 x 173 mm portrait shot-frame bound to @Frame (the graded pulled still for that beat), and a small masthead lockup frame at the top of the page bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The <<Beat>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long beat name binds without going overset. The board furniture (grid rule, caption bar, page ground) is already drawn into the template and is fixed on every page, so the only per-row imagery is the shot frame and the masthead wordmark. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up contact sheet: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-record-per-page sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-shot-per-page board is the correct, connector-doable shape (eight rows => an eight-page board), not a multi-up contact sheet. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@Frame, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded board frame AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every masthead without any free-form placement. Column names must exactly match the shot-list headers.

inputs.name: moonlit_shotlist.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: ShotNo,Beat,CameraNote,Timecode,FormatTag,@Frame,@Wordmark and 8 rows, one per requested board beat, in shot order. ShotNo is 01..08. Beat is the human beat name and MUST include at least one deliberately LONG name (e.g. 'The Clasp — Model Settles the Pendant at the Collarbone', ~48+ chars) alongside short ones (e.g. 'The Lift', 'First Glint') so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. CameraNote is a short NON-DIAGNOSTIC framing/move note per beat describing only the shot, framing or lens the camera is doing (e.g. 'lift off linen, wide', 'quarter turn, mid', 'crescent detail, macro', 'polished face, mid', 'slow rotation to back', 'raise to neckline', 'clasp at collarbone', 'settled at rest') — it MUST NOT name any lighting cast, colour temperature, exposure or grade direction, so the correction direction stays the freelancer's decision from the grey card rather than a value read off the CSV. Timecode is an approximate label string in the take ('00:03','00:08','00:14','00:19','00:24','00:29','00:34','00:39') — a client-supplied label the agent binds verbatim, NOT a value the agent measures. FormatTag is one of exactly two values: 'Lookbook Board' or 'Packaging Ref'. @Frame holds the agreed prepped board-frame filename for that beat (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_08_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded frame into that page. @Wordmark holds 'lunara_wordmark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized masthead lockup binds onto every page). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<ShotNo>>,<<Beat>>,<<CameraNote>>,<<Timecode>>,<<FormatTag>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight board pages (page-count = row-count gate). The @Frame column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned masthead lands on every page. Timecode/Beat/CameraNote are client copy bound verbatim (the timecodes are the client's shot-list labels, not agent measurements). The long clasp beat exercises the auto-fit name frame.

inputs.name: lunara_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat minimalist brand wordmark on a TRANSPARENT background: the word 'LUNARA' in an elegant high-contrast serif with a small crescent-moon glyph above the A, solid single-colour (soft charcoal) glyphs, crisp clean hard edges, high contrast, centred with a generous transparent margin all around, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, exported slightly oversized and off-centre, 2400x700 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, single-colour text art on transparent alpha so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds to strip the generous transparent margin, then a crisp contrast pass so the edges separate hard). Text-bearing wordmark -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms. It is a SUPPLIED asset only vectorized, never a from-scratch designed letterform.

outputs.name: LunaraSilver_MoonlitLaunch_ShotBoard_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED DELIVERABLE. A press-ready ~300 DPI A5 portrait (148 x 210 mm) + 3 mm bleed shot-board PDF, ONE shot per page, EIGHT pages (page-count = shot-list row-count = 8), exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge. Each page binds its ShotNo/Beat/CameraNote/Timecode/FormatTag verbatim from the shot list, drops that beat's grey-card-neutralized, house-graded board frame into the 130 x 173 mm portrait shot window (>=1535 x 2044 px so it prints >=300 DPI), and drops the vectorized wordmark into the masthead lockup. The board reads as one continuous grade across all eight pages. The 'hero' is simply page one of the merged board (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the beat selection, the crisp masthead — is the agent's, not a template default.

outputs.name: moonlit_frame_masters_cardbearing_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized full-frame masters (native ~3840x2160), one per pulled beat, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven to a clean neutral and the whole set matched to one shared white point and exposure feel while the silver stays true (bright, not blown; neutral, not blue). The grey card is RETAINED in frame in these masters — this is the grade-audit artifact the grader checks neutrality on (the card is cropped out of the board frames, so neutrality is graded here, on the retained card-bearing masters, not on the delivered board). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each frame.

outputs.name: moonlit_board_frames_x8
outputs.spec: Eight portrait board crops (frame_01_final.jpg ... frame_08_final.jpg), each cropped from the FULL-resolution card-bearing master to the 130 x 173 mm (~3:4) shot-window ratio with the grey card cropped OUT, held at >=1535 x 2044 px (target ~1620 x 2160, the maximum a portrait crop of the 4K frame holds) so each prints >=300 DPI in the window. These are the @Frame assets the merge resolves per row; the card-exclusion is checked here separately from the neutrality check on the masters.

outputs.name: moonlit_teaser_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: A full-length 9:16 vertical (1080x1920) reframe of the whole ~40s 4K take for the launch-announcement story — SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe only, no trim), produced by video_resize [A]. The 4K master's height carries a 9:16 crop of ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. Frame-accurate cuts, text overlays and motion graphics are the in-house Premiere finish, not claimed here.

outputs.name: lunara_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat wordmark cleaned and vectorized to a crisp SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds then a crisp contrast pass then trace), razor-sharp at any size, bound into every board masthead via the @Wordmark column and reusable on future covers.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns (NOT the primary output; the board PDF is): for each of the eight pulled beats, the white-balance temperature and tint and the exposure move that were applied, plus the final pixel size of each board frame, plus the single common house white point all eight were matched to. This makes 'the board is matched to one target' checkable — the corrections must be non-identical across the sun-out vs cloud-dimmed beats. It is an applied-settings log, never a measured/recovered pixel readout.

connector_workflow.note: Initialize a block upload of the client's single ~40s 4K take moonlit_take_4k.mp4 (media_type video/mp4) into the Lunara Silver Creative Cloud project folder. Returns the transfer document + presigned block URLs. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.
Finalize the take upload from step 1 into a real CC video assetId with a fetchable URL — the single source for both the pulled frames and the vertical teaser reframe.

Read the take's container metadata (duration ~40s, 3840x2160, frame rate) so the eight beat timecodes from the shot list sample sensibly across the real span. This is a metadata read, not a pixel measurement.

Pull the 'The Lift' beat near ~00:03 as a native 3840x2160 still. The agent chooses the exact frame — if the shot-list timecode lands on a motion-blurred transition, step to the clean adjacent frame (a soft frame prints muddy on the board). This beat is sun-out, warm and bright. [A].
Pull the 'The Turn' beat near ~00:08 as a native 3840x2160 still, choosing the sharp frame. Cloud passing here — cooler and dimmer than beat 1. [A].
Pull the 'Crescent Macro' beat near ~00:14 as a native still, the sharp frame. Hand shadows the piece — the darkest, most underexposed beat. [A].
Pull the 'First Glint' beat near ~00:19 as a native still, the sharp frame. Returning sun — bright with a hot specular glint on the polished silver that must be protected in the grade. [A].
Pull the 'Slow Rotation' beat near ~00:24 as a native still, the sharp frame. Near-neutral but flat and low-contrast. [A].
Pull the 'Raise to Neck' beat near ~00:29 as a native still, the sharp frame. Backlit, hazy and flat, slightly warm. [A].
Pull the 'The Clasp' beat near ~00:34 as a native still, the sharp frame (avoid the model's turn-in blur). Cool window fill on skin, a touch dim. [A].
Pull the 'Settled Rest' beat near ~00:39 as a native still, the sharp frame. Low warm sun — warm and slightly dark. [A].

ESTABLISH the house look on the sun-out lift beat and record it as the target the other seven must hit. Using the in-frame 18% grey card, COOL the warm cast (negative temperature) and set tint until the card reads true neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/whites so the bright frame holds without blowing the linen and the silver reads bright-not-blown. Reason to THIS card; report the move. Card RETAINED in frame — this is the card-bearing master. Single primitive-built adjustments call (not a preset, not auto_tone).

Crop the grey card OUT and reframe on the pendant to the 130 x 173 mm (~3:4) portrait board window, taken from the FULL 3840x2160 master so it holds ~1620x2160 (>=1535x2044, clears 300 DPI in the window). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand, never upscale. Report final px. Uploaded later as frame_01_final.jpg.

Grade the cloud-cooled turn beat to the SAME target — the OPPOSITE direction from beat 1: WARM it (positive temperature) and lift exposure until its grey card lands neutral on the common white point and its brightness matches the set. A blanket 'cool everything' pass fails here. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px (~1620x2160). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_02_final.jpg.

Grade the shadowed crescent macro — the biggest EXPOSURE lift in the set, plus a small WB nudge to seat its grey card on the common white point without going muddy or noisy in the lifted shadows. Tonal recovery dominates here. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_03_final.jpg.

Grade the first-glint beat: PULL highlights/whites down to save the hot specular on the polished silver first, then a small cool WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the common white point. Protecting the glint dominates. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_04_final.jpg.

Grade the flat rotation beat: its grey card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge to sit on the common white point — over-correcting pushes it off the set. The real work is tonal: add contrast/clarity to match the set's feel without clipping. Report the (small WB, tonal) move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_05_final.jpg.

Grade the backlit raise-to-neck beat: cut the haze with contrast, lift shadows carefully and cool the slight warmth so its grey card lands neutral on the common white point without crushing the flat backlit tone. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_06_final.jpg.

Grade the clasp beat: WARM the cool window fill and lift a touch until its grey card reads neutral on the common white point, watching the skin so it does not go muddy. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_07_final.jpg.

Grade the settled-rest beat: COOL the low-warm-sun cast and lift shadows so its grey card lands neutral on the common white point and it matches the set. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own retained grey card by its own decision. Report the move. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 3:4 board window from the full master at >=1535x2044 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. frame_08_final.jpg.

Reframe the whole ~40s 4K take to a clean full-frame 9:16 1080x1920 vertical for the launch-announcement story, SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe, no trim). The 4K height carries the 9:16 crop (~1215x2160) so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. [A] async-widget. FINAL video deliverable.
Initialize a block upload of the flat wordmark lunara_wordmark_flat.png (media_type image/png, transparent alpha) so it can be prepped and vectorized for the board masthead. Plumbing.
Finalize the wordmark upload from step 29 into a real CC image asset URL to drive the prep-before-trace chain.

Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the oversized/off-centre wordmark to the tight bounds of the glyphs (strips the generous transparent margin) so the trace sees only the lettering and crescent glyph, not empty canvas.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the single charcoal ink separates hard-edged from the transparent ground — a soft raster traces into ragged, doubled edges.

Trace the prepared flat wordmark into clean closed SVG paths (lunara_wordmark.svg) for a razor-sharp masthead lockup on every board page and future reuse. Vectorize of a SUPPLIED, prepared flat mark — no letterform is designed. FINAL vector deliverable, and the @Wordmark asset the merge binds.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: frame_01_final, frame_02_final, frame_03_final, frame_04_final, frame_05_final, frame_06_final, frame_07_final, frame_08_final, lunara_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight prepped board frames plus the vectorized wordmark so the merge can resolve them by the @Frame and @Wordmark columns. Files uploaded under the EXACT names the shot list references (frame_0N_final.jpg, lunara_wordmark.svg). Plumbing.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the shot list's @Frame / @Wordmark columns resolve to for each board page.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight shot-list rows (ShotNo/Beat/CameraNote/Timecode/FormatTag) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's graded board frame into the @Frame window AND the vectorized wordmark into the @Wordmark masthead — producing EXACTLY ONE board page per row (eight pages); the auto-fit frame shrinks the long clasp beat name. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-up contact sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.

Export the merged single-record pages to a press-ready ~300 DPI A5 + 3 mm bleed PDF with crop marks, one shot per page. The whole merged document exports as one file (no per-record named export; the hero is simply page one). Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. FINAL primary deliverable.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining anchored on the one client take. VIDEO SPINE: the 4K take is uploaded (1) and finalized (2 -> take_asset); video_metadata (3) reads its duration/format so the eight beat timecodes sample across the real ~40s. Eight video_render_frame pulls (4-11) each pull a DIFFERENT beat at a DIFFERENT chosen timecode from take_asset (the creative selection the agent owns — which beat, which sharp frame), yielding native 3840x2160 stills frame_01_raw..frame_08_raw. Each raw frame drives its own two-step grade sub-chain: an image_apply_adjustments neutralization to the in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per beat: cool the sun-out lift 12, warm+lift the cloud-cooled turn 14, big exposure lift on the shadowed macro 16, protect the specular glint 18, small-WB+tonal on the flat rotation 20, de-haze the backlit raise 22, warm the cool clasp 24, cool the warm rest 26) whose output is the RETAINED card-bearing master, followed by an image_crop_and_resize (13,15,17,19,21,23,25,27) that crops the grey card OUT and reframes to the 3:4 board window from the FULL master at >=1535x2044 px. Every neutralization is driven to that frame's own grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. video_resize (28) reframes take_asset to the same-runtime 1080x1920 vertical teaser. WORDMARK BRANCH: upload-init (29) -> finalize (30 -> wordmark_asset) -> crop_to_bounds (31) -> crisp adjustments (32) -> image_vectorize (33 -> lunara_wordmark.svg). CONVERGENCE: the eight board frames and the vectorized wordmark fan into the merge upload session (34) -> finalize (35 -> merge_asset_urns) -> document_merge_data_layout (36), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the shot-list CSV and emits one board page per row resolving BOTH @Frame and @Wordmark; the merged set exports to the per-shot press PDF (37). The only non-chained calls are the three standard upload-init idioms (1,29,34), each immediately consumed by its finalize; everything else sets inputs_from to a producing step's output.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 37 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (video [A] frame-pull/reframe + [C] metadata, image raster [C], InDesign merge [T]/[C]) — well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the three upload idioms (6 plumbing calls), leaving 31 difficulty-bearing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: the core is eight DIFFERENT reasoned grade decisions, in different directions, all forced to converge on one measurable target (the static in-frame 18% grey card) even though the eight beats were pulled from a single take whose light drifts — cool the sun-out beats, warm the cloud-dimmed beats, lift the shadowed macro hardest, protect the specular glint, hold the near-neutral flat beat on WB but add tone — so a blanket batch correction or per-frame auto-tone visibly fails to match at the cards. Layered on top: a genuine constraint-reasoning problem around a tool limit — a 130 x 173 mm portrait print window derived from a 16:9 4K still can ONLY be met by cropping the vertical strip from the FULL 3840x2160 frame (max ~1620x2160), which just clears the ~1535x2044 300 DPI floor; grading on a downscaled proxy or stretching a landscape frame to fill the portrait window falls under and prints soft, and neither the connector nor the agent may upscale. The same camera-scale reasoning governs the video_resize teaser (a 9:16 crop of the 4K height holds >=1080 width, so 1080x1920 is honest; a 1080p source could not deliver it). Plus prep-before-trace wordmark discipline (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> vectorize) and a two-image-column one-file-per-row merge into a hand-authored single-record template. Respects every hard limit: video_render_frame pulls native stills (no upscale), video_resize is same-runtime reframe (no trim, no upscale), image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract', no generative fill/expand/text-to-image/object-removal/from-scratch art, no image_fill_area, no image_apply_color_overlay, no auto_tone in the correct path (auto_tone is the named trap), no >90deg hsl rotation, convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used, and the merge places one record per page (no N-up). Deprecated tools (image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast) are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the eight board pages must read as ONE continuous grade — every pulled frame's in-frame 18% grey card driven to one common white point with the set on one exposure feel — and because the beats were pulled from a single take whose light drifts, each needs its OWN opposite-direction correction; running one global correction or per-frame auto_tone (which keys off each frame's own histogram) leaves the sun-out and cloud-dimmed beats disagreeing at the grey cards and the board is rejected, and the agent must REPORT the per-frame temperature/tint/exposure move and final pixel size so 'matched' is auditable rather than asserted. Two further checkable gates back it: every board frame must clear >=1535x2044 px (so it prints >=300 DPI in the 130 x 173 mm window) and the merged PDF page-count must equal the shot-list row-count (8), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable common white point across eight frames pulled from one changing-light take, each requiring a different, sometimes opposite correction reasoned to its own retained grey card — not one set of sliders; (2) constraint-reasoning around a tool limitation — a portrait print frame can only be derived from the landscape 4K still by cropping the vertical strip from the FULL-resolution frame so it barely clears the 300 DPI floor, with no upscaling permitted anywhere (the same reasoning that makes the 1080x1920 teaser honest only because the source is 4K); plus prep-before-trace wordmark discipline. TRAP (the brief does not disclose it — it states the goal 'the board has to read as one continuous piece' and leaves the method to the agent): the naive path auto-tones or globally corrects each pulled frame so each looks fine alone, which passes a thumbnail but drifts apart at the grey cards and fails the one-white-point gate; a second pitfall is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference) — which is why neutrality is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing masters and card-exclusion is checked separately on the board frames; a third is grading on a downscaled proxy or stretching a landscape frame to fill the portrait window, dropping under the print floor. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, agent never measures): every grey card neutral (R=G=B) at the common white point on the eight retained masters with per-frame WB/exposure reported; every board frame >=1535x2044 px with final px reported; the teaser exactly 1080x1920 at the take's full runtime; the wordmark a crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A5 board page per shot-list row.
